📌 Hidden Fees: Why “Zero Fee” Doesn’t Mean Free

Main Points
⏺ Crypto trade costs can hide in spreads, slippage, and execution routes
⏺ “No fee” often means the cost moves somewhere else
⏺ This post explains how to see the real price of an action

1️⃣ Spread — the gap between buy and sell price can already be your first hidden cost.
2️⃣ Slippage — weaker liquidity pushes your final price away from the quote.
3️⃣ Routing — an app or aggregator may choose a route that benefits it more than you.
4️⃣ Network Costs — even if the platform charges no fee, gas is still a real expense.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — compare final received amounts, check multiple routes, and don’t trust “0% fee” alone.

Final Thoughts

Trades are rarely free. If the fee isn’t visible in one line, it may live inside price, routing, or liquidity.

Zelensky: Western Allies Failed to Warn Kyiv Before Russian Ballistic Missile Attack


Zelensky has criticized the lack of advance warning from Western partners before a Russian ballistic missile attack struck civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, raising fresh questions about intelligence-sharing as tensions between Washington and Kyiv continue to grow.

Zelensky said five ballistic missiles hit civilian infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital on Monday, October 12. 

He described the strike as particularly reprehensible and stressed that timely intelligence about Russian missile launches can help save lives. “Intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives, and this is one of the most critical issues,” Zelensky said in a statement published on social media. 

He added that Ukraine had received no early warning from its partners before the attack. The Ukrainian leader’s remarks came amid growing uncertainty over U.S. support, following reports that American officials had threatened to suspend intelligence cooperation with Kyiv. 

The warnings reportedly came as the Trump administration pressed Ukraine to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries. 

Despite the concerns, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha indicated that intelligence cooperation with the United States was continuing. He suggested that the absence of a warning before the Kyiv strike could be linked to the particular type of Russian weapon used. The dispute highlights the importance of intelligence-sharing beyond identifying targets for Ukrainian strikes against Russia. 

Ukrainian military officials have said that information from the United States is particularly valuable for detecting ballistic missile launches and monitoring the takeoff of Russian long-range bombers, giving civilians and emergency services a chance to prepare.

Zelensky also accused Moscow of disregarding Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire. According to the Ukrainian president, Kyiv had refrained from attacking Russian oil refineries and energy facilities for two days after the announcement, while Russian forces continued striking Ukrainian infrastructure.

He said 19 Ukrainian regions had come under attack during that period, adding that Russian forces had made clear they were not prepared to stop their bombardment.

Ukraine, Zelensky said, remained willing to take reciprocal steps toward de-escalation but needed effective international pressure on Moscow to secure meaningful results. 

He warned that reducing assistance to Ukraine or making it more difficult to protect civilians from ballistic missiles would undermine efforts to achieve peace.

The latest developments underscore the challenges facing Western allies as they balance diplomatic efforts to end the war with continued military and intelligence support for Kyiv. 

While Ukrainian officials say cooperation with Washington remains active, Zelensky’s comments reveal the potentially deadly consequences when early-warning information does not reach Ukrainian authorities in time.

🔖 Australia proposes new crypto exchange rules for 2027 

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
